meta.title: DMV Plant Health Care Treatment Planner
meta.source: DMV PHC Knowledge Base v1.0 (Aug 2026), normalized for the app
meta.disclaimer: Framework for treatment planning only. No rates are provided; product selection, rates, and timing must follow the label. Confirm diagnosis and current VA/MD/DC regulations before application.

conditions.name: Boxwood Blight
conditions.hostNote: All Buxus species; pachysandra occasionally infected.
symptoms: Circular tan to brown leaf spots with dark borders
Rapid, complete defoliation within days to weeks in humid weather
Black streaks and cankers on green stems
White spore masses on undersides of fresh lesions (hand lens)
biology: Spreads by water splash, tools, clothing, and infected nursery stock
Spores survive in soil and leaf debris 5+ years
Favored by temperatures above 60°F with wet leaves
conditions.peakNote: Most aggressive June–September in the DMV.

treatments.title: Preventive fungicide program
treatments.frequency: Every 7–14 days during warm, wet high-risk periods
treatments.purpose: Protects healthy foliage from new infection. Does not cure infected tissue.
notes: Rotate FRAC groups every 2–3 applications: chlorothalonil (M5), tebuconazole / propiconazole (3), thiophanate-methyl (1)
Avoid propiconazole on heat-stressed plants

treatments.title: Remove and destroy infected plants and debris
treatments.purpose: Removes the spore source. Infected material is bagged and removed, never composted.
notes: Sanitize tools with 70% isopropyl alcohol or 1:9 bleach between cuts
Clean clothing and equipment before leaving the site

treatments.title: Irrigation and mulch adjustments
treatments.purpose: Switching to drip or early-morning watering and adding 2–4 in. of mulch reduces leaf wetness and splash spread.

treatments.title: Replace with resistant cultivars or alternatives
treatments.purpose: Resistant boxwood (e.g., 'Winter Gem', 'Green Mountain', 'Justin Brouwers') or non-boxwood alternatives such as Ilex crenata end the cycle.

regulatory.text: VDACS runs a Voluntary Boxwood Blight Cleanliness Program for nurseries; commercial movement of infected stock is regulated.

conditions.name: Anthracnose
symptoms: Dogwood: tan blotches with purple borders, shoot blight, sprouts low on the trunk; can kill trees
Oak: irregular brown blotches along veins, leaf distortion, early drop
Sycamore: spring bud and shoot blight, papery brown leaves, heavy defoliation in cold wet springs
biology: Cool (below 60°F), wet weather during leaf emergence drives infection
Overwinters in twig cankers and fallen leaves

treatments.title: Spring protective fungicide program
treatments.frequency: 2–3 applications at 7–14 day intervals from bud break through leaf expansion
treatments.purpose: Protects new leaves and shoots during the infection window.
notes: Myclobutanil (FRAC 3), propiconazole (FRAC 3), or thiophanate-methyl (FRAC 1)

treatments.title: Systemic fungicide injection for high-value trees
treatments.purpose: Delivers protection directly into the tree. Suited to large or high-value specimens that are hard to spray.
notes: Propiconazole injection per KB; confirm label for host and timing

treatments.title: Leaf litter cleanup and dead twig pruning
treatments.purpose: Removes overwintering infection sources.

treatments.title: Avoid overhead irrigation during leaf-out
treatments.purpose: Reduces leaf wetness during the spring infection period.

conditions.name: Phytophthora Root & Crown Rot
conditions.hostNote: Dogwood, rhododendron, azalea, boxwood, holly, and many others.
symptoms: Yellowing or wilting despite adequate soil moisture
Brown, water-soaked crown and root tissue
Dark discoloration beneath bark at the soil line
Brown/black roots with no white root tips
biology: Favored by poorly drained, compacted, heavy clay soils and overwatering
Water mold that spreads in soil and irrigation water

treatments.title: Drainage and irrigation correction
treatments.purpose: Reducing watering frequency and improving drainage is the foundation of recovery.
notes: Raise planting grade if needed; let soil dry between waterings

treatments.title: Systemic root-protection soil drench
treatments.purpose: Suppresses the root pathogen and protects new roots. Preventive / suppressive, not curative.
notes: Mefenoxam / metalaxyl (FRAC 4, phenylamide) or phosphonates: fosetyl-Al, phosphorous acid (FRAC P07)

treatments.title: Phosphonate trunk injection or basal bark treatment
treatments.purpose: Delivers root-protecting phosphonate directly into the tree's vascular system.
notes: Phosphite products are also labeled as basal bark sprays; confirm label

treatments.title: Replant planning
treatments.purpose: Avoid replanting susceptible species in infested soil without remediation.

reviewFlags: Source KB grouped mefenoxam/metalaxyl with phosphonates. They are phenylamides (FRAC 4); phosphonates are FRAC P07 (formerly 33). Corrected here.

conditions.name: Powdery Mildew
symptoms: White powdery coating on leaf surfaces
Distorted, stunted new growth
Early leaf drop in severe cases
biology: Rarely kills established plants; mainly an appearance and vigor problem

treatments.title: Protective fungicide program
treatments.frequency: At first sign, repeat per label
treatments.purpose: Protects foliage and stops spread to new leaves.
notes: Trifloxystrobin (FRAC 11), myclobutanil (FRAC 3), bicarbonate products

treatments.title: Airflow pruning and fertility adjustment
treatments.purpose: Thinning for air movement and avoiding excess nitrogen reduces mildew pressure.

treatments.title: Resistant cultivar selection
treatments.purpose: Resistant cultivars (e.g., dogwood 'Stellar Pink', 'Celestial') for new plantings.

reviewFlags: Source KB gives no timing. Months and 'at first sign' timing were added and need review.

conditions.name: Cedar-Apple Rust
conditions.hostNote: Alternates between Eastern red cedar and apple / crabapple / hawthorn.
symptoms: Orange gelatinous horns on cedar galls in early spring
Bright orange-yellow spots on apple/crabapple leaves
Tube-like structures on leaf undersides

treatments.title: Bloom-period protective fungicide on apple-family hosts
treatments.purpose: Protects leaves during the spring infection window.
notes: Myclobutanil per KB; KB also lists triadimefon (verify current registration)

treatments.title: Remove galls from cedars
treatments.purpose: Removing galls in late winter, before wet weather, eliminates the spring spore source.

treatments.title: Resistant crabapple selection
treatments.purpose: Choose rust-resistant crabapple cultivars for new plantings.

reviewFlags: Triadimefon availability for ornamentals should be verified.

conditions.name: Verticillium Wilt
symptoms: Sudden wilting and death of one or more branches (flagging)
Olive-green to brown streaking in sapwood (diagnostic)
One-sided canopy death; wilted leaves stay attached

treatments.title: Lab confirmation
treatments.purpose: Confirms the diagnosis before investing in a long-term care plan.
notes: VCE Plant Disease Clinic (KB lists $35 submission fee; verify)

treatments.title: Remove affected branches to healthy wood
treatments.purpose: Removes dying limbs and reduces stress on the tree.

treatments.title: Vigor support: fertilization and irrigation
treatments.purpose: A well-nourished, well-watered tree can wall off the infection.
notes: Avoid root wounding; do not replant susceptible species in infested soil

conditions.name: Diplodia Tip Blight
conditions.hostNote: Austrian pine most susceptible; also Scotch and Eastern white pine.
symptoms: New shoots brown and die in spring while older needles stay green
Resinous stem cankers
Small black fruiting bodies at needle and cone bases
Worst on the lower two-thirds of the tree

treatments.title: Three-spray spring protection program
treatments.frequency: Bud swell, bud break, and 2 weeks after bud break
treatments.purpose: Protects each flush of new shoots during infection.
notes: Chlorothalonil or propiconazole

treatments.title: Prune out infected tips in dry weather
treatments.purpose: Reduces spore load. Tools are sanitized between cuts.

treatments.title: Removal of heavily infected trees
treatments.purpose: Protects neighboring pines when a tree is beyond recovery.

conditions.name: Fire Blight
symptoms: Shoot tips die and bend into a shepherd's crook
Leaves brown but stay attached, as if scorched
Amber bacterial ooze from cankers in humid weather
Blossoms wilt; fruit mummifies
biology: Spread by pollinators, rain splash, and pruning tools
Infects blossoms and wounds in warm (65–86°F), wet weather at bloom

treatments.title: Sanitation pruning 6–12 in. below symptoms
treatments.purpose: Removes active cankers. Tools are sterilized between every cut and debris is removed from site.
notes: Prune in dry weather; dormant-season pruning of cankers preferred

treatments.title: Bloom-period protective bactericide sprays
treatments.purpose: Protects blossoms during the infection window.
notes: Copper products; streptomycin only where labeled for the site (resistance documented)

treatments.title: Canker suppression with phosphorous acid
treatments.purpose: Suppressive support for canker management.
notes: Phosphorous acid products; confirm label for application method

reviewFlags: Streptomycin labeling for landscape ornamentals varies; verify before recommending.

conditions.name: Bacterial Leaf Scorch
conditions.hostNote: Red, pin, and scarlet oaks most susceptible.
symptoms: Irregular brown leaf-margin scorch from mid-summer to fall
Yellow to red band between brown and green tissue (oak)
Progresses branch by branch over years
biology: Spread by leafhoppers and spittlebugs, not pruning tools
Lives in the water-conducting tissue; no cure

treatments.title: Lab confirmation (ELISA/PCR)
treatments.purpose: Confirms the infection. Trees should not be treated or removed on suspicion alone.

treatments.title: Annual antibiotic trunk injection
treatments.purpose: Suppresses symptoms and slows decline. Does not eliminate the bacteria.
notes: Oxytetracycline (micro or macro injection systems)

treatments.title: Vigor program: irrigation, soil care, fertilization
treatments.purpose: Reduces stress so the tree tolerates infection longer.

treatments.title: Removal of severely affected trees
treatments.purpose: When decline is advanced, removal and replanting is the long-term solution.

conditions.name: Wetwood / Slime Flux
symptoms: Foul-smelling, foamy or slimy seepage from wounds or cracks
Vertical gray-brown streaks on bark
Internal wood discoloration

treatments.title: Stress reduction and wound avoidance
treatments.purpose: A healthy tree contains the condition.

treatments.title: Improve drainage on saturated soils
treatments.purpose: Corrects a common contributing factor.

treatments.title: Structural monitoring
treatments.purpose: Removal is only needed if structural integrity is compromised.

warnings: Drain tubes are no longer recommended by most authorities.

conditions.name: Ash Yellows
symptoms: Witches' brooms (clusters of stunted shoots)
Small, yellowish leaves
Early fall color and leaf drop
Slow, progressive decline

treatments.title: Confirm diagnosis (rule out EAB)
treatments.purpose: Ash yellows is often confused with emerald ash borer.

treatments.title: Suppressive antibiotic injection
treatments.purpose: May temporarily suppress symptoms.
notes: Oxytetracycline

treatments.title: Removal and replacement with non-ash species
treatments.purpose: The long-term solution given EAB pressure.

conditions.name: Tobacco Rattle Virus
symptoms: Mosaic, ring spot, or line patterns on leaves
Stunting and distorted growth

treatments.title: Remove infected plants
treatments.purpose: Eliminates the infection source.

warnings: The virus is spread by soil nematodes (Trichodorus). Soil fumigation is generally impractical and highly regulated in landscapes.
reviewFlags: Source KB suggested soil fumigants for vector control. Removed as a treatment option.

conditions.name: Drought Stress
symptoms: Leaf margin and tip scorch
Wilting, leaf curl
Early fall color
Uniform pattern across the canopy that tracks the weather

treatments.title: Deep, infrequent watering plan
treatments.purpose: About 1 in. of water per week during drought, applied deeply.

treatments.title: Root zone mulching and decompaction
treatments.purpose: 3–4 in. of mulch over the root zone conserves moisture.

conditions.name: Winter Injury / Freeze Damage
symptoms: Branch dieback
Frost cracks in bark
Bud death
Browning of evergreen foliage (desiccation)

treatments.title: Late-season deep watering
treatments.purpose: Hydrated plants resist winter desiccation.

treatments.title: Anti-desiccant spray on evergreens
treatments.purpose: Reduces winter moisture loss from foliage.

treatments.title: Fertility timing adjustment
treatments.purpose: Avoiding late-season fertilization prevents tender growth going into winter.

conditions.name: Nutrient Deficiency (Iron / Manganese / Nitrogen)
conditions.hostNote: Iron chlorosis common on pin oak and sweetgum in high-pH soils.
symptoms: Yellowing between veins on new growth (iron / manganese)
Overall pale green or yellow foliage, slow growth (nitrogen)

treatments.title: Soil test
treatments.purpose: Identifies pH and the actual deficiency (iron vs. manganese need testing to tell apart).

treatments.title: Soil acidification and nutrient program
treatments.purpose: Corrects pH and supplies nutrients per soil test.

treatments.title: Micronutrient trunk injection
treatments.purpose: Fast greening for trees that cannot take up iron or manganese from high-pH soil.
notes: Chelated iron / manganese injection or drench

conditions.name: Soil Compaction
symptoms: Poor growth, stunting
Leaf scorch and dieback
Waterlogging after rain

treatments.title: Air-spade root zone decompaction
treatments.purpose: Breaks up compacted soil without damaging roots.

treatments.title: Vertical mulching / radial aeration
treatments.purpose: Opens channels for air, water, and roots.

treatments.title: Organic matter amendment
treatments.purpose: Improves soil structure over time.

conditions.name: Girdling Roots
symptoms: Gradual crown thinning from the top down
No visible root flare; flat-sided trunk

treatments.title: Root collar excavation
treatments.purpose: Exposes the root flare to find girdling roots.

treatments.title: Girdling root removal
treatments.purpose: Removes roots crossing the trunk before they cause serious damage.

conditions.name: Road Salt Damage
symptoms: Spring leaf margin scorch
Browning of roadside evergreens
Dieback on the road-facing side

treatments.title: Spring soil flushing
treatments.purpose: Deep irrigation leaches salt from the root zone.

treatments.title: De-icer practice changes
treatments.purpose: Reducing sodium chloride use near plantings limits future injury.

treatments.title: Salt-tolerant species for roadside plantings
treatments.purpose: Long-term fix for exposed sites.

reviewFlags: Source KB says 'use calcium chloride alternatives'. Ambiguous wording; rephrased.

conditions.name: Over / Under Irrigation
symptoms: Overwatering: yellowing, root rot, symptoms similar to Phytophthora
Underwatering: scorch, early leaf drop, decline

treatments.title: Irrigation audit and adjustment
treatments.purpose: Check soil moisture before watering; adjust schedules to plant needs.

conditions.name: Emerald Ash Borer (EAB)
symptoms: D-shaped exit holes 3–4 mm (diagnostic)
S-shaped larval galleries under bark
Crown dieback from the top down
Sprouting from trunk and limbs
Woodpecker damage and bark flaking
biology: Small trees can die within 1–2 years; large trees within 3–4 years

treatments.title: Systemic trunk injection (2–3 year protection)
treatments.purpose: The most effective EAB protection, delivered directly into the tree after leaf-out.
notes: Emamectin benzoate (e.g., TREE-äge); check RUP status of formulation

treatments.title: Systemic soil drench (annual)
treatments.purpose: Annual protection option, best on smaller trees.
notes: Imidacloprid; less effective on large trees

treatments.title: Systemic basal bark spray (annual)
treatments.purpose: Fast-acting, no-drill annual protection.
notes: Dinotefuran (soil drench also an option)

treatments.title: Removal and replacement
treatments.purpose: Recommended for trees with more than 50% crown loss.

costShare.text: Virginia DOF EAB Treatment Cost-Share: up to 70% cost offset for eligible trees.
Maryland 50/50 cost-share for treatments on public land.

regulatory.text: Treatment threshold per KB: under 30% crown loss (VA guidance), under 50–60% (MD guidance). Do not treat above 50% loss.

reviewFlags: KB cites a federal interstate EAB quarantine; USDA-APHIS ended the federal domestic EAB quarantine in Jan 2021. Verify current VA/MD quarantine status.
Cost-share percentages and DBH minimums need current-year verification.

conditions.name: Bronze Birch Borer
conditions.hostNote: White/paper birch most susceptible; river birch most tolerant.
symptoms: D-shaped exit holes (smaller than EAB)
Serpentine galleries under bark
Dieback from the crown down
Yellow, sparse foliage

treatments.title: Preventive systemic soil drench
treatments.purpose: Protects against new borer attack.
notes: Imidacloprid

treatments.title: Watering and mulching for vigor
treatments.purpose: Stressed birch attract borers; healthy birch resist them.

treatments.title: Plant resistant species
treatments.purpose: River birch is the most borer-tolerant option.

conditions.name: Two-Lined Chestnut Borer
conditions.hostNote: Oaks stressed by drought or defoliation.
symptoms: Dieback from branch tips
Small metallic green beetles with two lines
S-shaped galleries under bark of dying branches

treatments.title: Preventive systemic treatment for high-value oaks
treatments.purpose: Protects at-risk trees from borer attack.
notes: Imidacloprid

treatments.title: Drought stress relief and vigor care
treatments.purpose: Addresses the stress that attracts the borer.

treatments.title: Remove infested branches
treatments.purpose: Removes developing larvae.

reviewFlags: Source KB gives no timing for preventive treatment; spring months added.

conditions.name: Dogwood Borer
symptoms: Frass and gumming at trunk base and scaffold limbs
Rough, swollen callus at entry sites
Tunneling under bark

treatments.title: Protective trunk spray program
treatments.purpose: Protects bark during adult egg-laying.
notes: Permethrin or bifenthrin

treatments.title: Trunk flare protection (mulch ring)
treatments.purpose: Prevents mower and trimmer wounds, the main entry point.

conditions.name: Hemlock Woolly Adelgid (HWA)
symptoms: White, cottony egg sacs at needle bases on twig undersides (diagnostic)
Needles turn gray-green and drop
Twig death progressing from the bottom up
biology: Two generations per year; dormant (not feeding) July–September
Untreated trees can die in 4–6 years
conditions.noTreatmentReason: Adelgids are dormant and not feeding July–September.

treatments.title: Long-term systemic soil treatment (4–7 years)
treatments.purpose: Long-lasting protection. Large trees take about 3 months to take it up.
notes: Imidacloprid soil drench or soil injection

treatments.title: Fast-acting systemic basal bark spray
treatments.purpose: Knocks down heavy infestations within days. Often paired with the long-term treatment.
notes: Dinotefuran (also drench or injection)

treatments.title: Direct systemic trunk injection
treatments.purpose: Treatment directly into the tree where soil or bark treatment is not practical.
notes: Imidacloprid or dinotefuran injection

treatments.title: Horticultural oil spray (small trees)
treatments.purpose: Contact control for small trees where complete coverage is possible.
notes: 1% summer rate / 2% winter rate per KB; follow label

costShare.text: Virginia DOF Hemlock Woolly Adelgid Treatment Cost-Share Program.

conditions.name: Elongate Hemlock Scale
symptoms: Flat, elongate brown/tan scales on needle undersides
Yellow stippling and needle drop
Often found together with HWA

treatments.title: Horticultural oil spray
treatments.purpose: Contact control of scale and crawlers.

treatments.title: Systemic soil drench or basal bark spray
treatments.purpose: Systemic control inside the needles.
notes: Dinotefuran preferred; imidacloprid listed in KB but generally weak on armored scale

treatments.title: Crawler-stage growth-regulator spray
treatments.purpose: Targets crawlers as they emerge.
notes: Pyriproxyfen (IGR)

reviewFlags: Imidacloprid efficacy on armored scales is limited; KB lists it as an option.

conditions.name: Crapemyrtle Bark Scale (CMBS)
symptoms: White/gray waxy crust on trunk and limbs (diagnostic)
Heavy black sooty mold on bark
Pink fluid when scale is crushed
Reduced flowering

treatments.title: Spring systemic soil drench
treatments.purpose: The most effective approach. Systemic protection through the season.
notes: Imidacloprid, dinotefuran, clothianidin, or thiamethoxam

treatments.title: Dormant oil bark spray
treatments.purpose: Smothers overwintering scale; needs thorough bark coverage.

treatments.title: Crawler-stage growth-regulator spray
treatments.purpose: Targets crawlers. Not applied during bloom.
notes: Pyriproxyfen (IGR)

treatments.title: Bark scrubbing
treatments.purpose: Soft brush and dilute soap for small infestations; also removes sooty mold.

conditions.name: Beech Scale / Beech Bark Disease
symptoms: White woolly material on trunk and limbs
Cankers, oozing, tarry spots on bark
Crown dieback

treatments.title: Trunk scrubbing
treatments.purpose: Removes scale on small infestations.

treatments.title: Horticultural oil or soap bark spray
treatments.purpose: Controls scale on accessible bark.

treatments.title: Vigor support
treatments.purpose: Healthy trees resist infection longer.

conditions.name: Aphids
symptoms: Soft-bodied insects in colonies on new growth or bark
Sticky honeydew and black sooty mold below
Curled, distorted leaves

treatments.title: Horticultural oil or insecticidal soap
treatments.purpose: Contact control that spares most beneficial insects.

treatments.title: Systemic treatment for persistent infestations
treatments.purpose: Season-long control on heavily affected plants.
notes: Imidacloprid or dinotefuran

treatments.title: Beneficial insect conservation and water spray
treatments.purpose: Lady beetles and lacewings plus water sprays knock colonies down.

conditions.name: Spotted Lanternfly (SLF)
symptoms: Adults: gray wings with black spots, red hindwings
Nymphs: black with white spots, later red
Gray, mud-like egg masses on bark and outdoor objects
Honeydew and sooty mold below feeding sites

treatments.title: Egg mass scraping
treatments.purpose: Each egg mass destroyed removes 30–50 future insects.

treatments.title: Circle traps on trunks
treatments.purpose: Chemical-free capture of nymphs and adults climbing the trunk.

treatments.title: Tree of heaven removal
treatments.purpose: Removes the preferred breeding host.

treatments.title: Systemic protection for high-value trees
treatments.purpose: Protects valued trees during peak feeding.
notes: Dinotefuran or imidacloprid

treatments.title: Knockdown spray
treatments.purpose: Contact control of heavy populations.
notes: Bifenthrin or spinosad

regulatory.text: DC DOEE discourages broad pesticide use for SLF. Lead with mechanical control, reporting, and tree of heaven removal.
SLF quarantine covers 20+ counties; businesses moving regulated articles need a compliance agreement/permit. Report to dontbug.md@maryland.gov.
Intrastate quarantine reported repealed March 2025; interstate movement rules remain. Reporting encouraged in new counties.

reviewFlags: Verify VA quarantine repeal and current MD quarantine county list.

conditions.name: Japanese Beetle
symptoms: Metallic green/copper beetles about 1/2 in. long
Leaves skeletonized from the top of the plant down
Adults feed in groups June–August

treatments.title: Preventive systemic treatment
treatments.purpose: In place before adults emerge.
notes: Imidacloprid or dinotefuran; NOT on linden or other bee-attractive hosts before or during bloom

treatments.title: Contact spray during feeding
treatments.purpose: Knocks down active feeding adults.
notes: Bifenthrin, carbaryl, or other pyrethroids

reviewFlags: KB listed halofenozide for grubs. It is discontinued and has been removed.

conditions.name: Bagworm
symptoms: Cone-shaped silk bags (1–1.5 in.) covered in plant material
Severe defoliation of evergreens
200–1,000 eggs overwinter in each bag

treatments.title: Bag removal before hatch
treatments.purpose: Removes overwintering eggs before they hatch.

treatments.title: Early-season caterpillar spray
treatments.purpose: Targets small caterpillars, including low-impact biological options.
notes: Bt kurstaki, spinosad, or pyrethroids; ineffective once bags exceed 1/2 in.

conditions.name: Fall Webworm
symptoms: Large silk webs enclosing branch-tip foliage in late summer–fall
Hairy caterpillars feeding inside webs

treatments.title: Web and branch removal
treatments.purpose: Removes caterpillars and webs.

treatments.title: Early-stage caterpillar spray
treatments.purpose: Biological or low-impact control before webs get large.
notes: Bt or spinosad

conditions.name: Spongy Moth (formerly Gypsy Moth)
symptoms: Hairy caterpillars 2–3 in. with blue and red spots
Tan egg masses on bark and structures
Complete defoliation of large oaks

treatments.title: Early-instar caterpillar spray
treatments.purpose: Targets young caterpillars with biological or low-impact products.
notes: Bt kurstaki (most recommended), spinosad; diflubenzuron is broad-spectrum, so use caution near water

treatments.title: Egg mass removal
treatments.purpose: Scrape egg masses into soapy water before spring hatch.

treatments.title: Burlap trunk bands
treatments.purpose: Traps caterpillars that hide during the day; checked and cleared regularly.

conditions.name: Two-Spotted Spider Mite
symptoms: Fine yellow/white stippling on leaves
Fine webbing on leaf undersides
Tiny mites visible with a hand lens
Outbreaks in hot, dry weather

treatments.title: Horticultural oil or soap spray
treatments.purpose: Contact control with thorough leaf-underside coverage.

treatments.title: Targeted miticide program
treatments.purpose: Rotated miticides for heavy populations.
notes: Bifenazate, abamectin, spiromesifen; rotate modes of action; avoid pyrethroids (mite flare)

treatments.title: Moisture management
treatments.purpose: Drought-stressed plants suffer worse outbreaks.

conditions.name: Spruce Spider Mite
symptoms: Stippling and bronzing of needles
Green mites and eggs on needles in cool seasons
Webbing in heavy infestations
conditions.noTreatmentReason: Spruce spider mite is a cool-season mite and is inactive in summer heat.

treatments.title: Dormant oil before bud break
treatments.purpose: Smothers overwintering eggs.

treatments.title: Spring / fall miticide
treatments.purpose: Controls active populations during cool seasons.

jurisdictions.name: Virginia
notes: Commercial applications require a Virginia Pesticide Business License (or employment by a licensed firm).
Records retained 2 years minimum.
jurisdictions.nearWater: Chesapeake Bay Preservation Act: Resource Protection Areas include a 100-ft buffer from tidal wetlands and shorelines. Limit applications and follow label setbacks.
jurisdictions.sensitiveSite: Follow label and local ordinance notification requirements.

jurisdictions.name: Maryland
notes: Records retained 2 years minimum.
jurisdictions.nearWater: Chesapeake Bay Critical Area (1,000 ft from tidal waters) carries enhanced restrictions and BMPs; Clean Streams Law prohibits applications that cause water quality violations.
jurisdictions.sensitiveSite: Schools and childcare facilities must follow IPM programs: 24-hour advance notification to parents and post-application notification within 24 hours.
jurisdictions.neonicotinoid: Maryland restricts neonicotinoids (imidacloprid, dinotefuran, clothianidin, thiamethoxam). Applications must be made by a certified applicator. Verify current product status.

jurisdictions.name: District of Columbia
notes: Requires DOEE Certified Applicator status, a DC Basic Business License, and a DOEE photo ID carried during all applications.
IPM-first approach expected on public spaces.
Records retained 2 years minimum.
jurisdictions.nearWater: Strict buffers near the Anacostia River, Rock Creek, and Potomac tributaries. DC municipal buffers may exceed label requirements.
jurisdictions.sensitiveSite: Enhanced restrictions and pre-notification for schools, daycares, and parks.
